title: tree-sitter
subtitle: tree-sitter parses a multi-language monorepo into the chunks and edges behind my code search and dependency graph.

stats.label: lines, the longest unit kept whole

lede: FAFOHive serves AI agents that ask questions about a large multi-language monorepo, and I wanted their answers to come from the code's structure. Embeddings of arbitrary line windows give agents half a function and a guess. I decided to parse every file with tree-sitter and use the syntax tree twice: to cut code into meaningful chunks for search, and to extract the dependency graph the code tools traverse. The chunker uses pinned grammars for Rust, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C, C++, Go and Java and cuts along function, class and module boundaries. A long unit splits into overlapping sub-chunks, so a long function stays findable without becoming one diluted vector. Files in other languages go through a plain chunker.
quote: I give AI agents computed facts about code and limit the model to explaining them.
evidence: Code intelligence for AI agents: a 19,000-file multi-language monorepo parsed with tree-sitter into 294,000 syntax-aligned chunks for code search.
Static dependency analysis: calls, imports and implementations extracted into a generation-versioned graph whose edges appear only when both ends are indexed.
Evidence-grounded LLM output: dependency tracing by bounded search in SQL, with a model allowed to narrate only edges the graph holds.
author: Corey James
